audit.summary: Change class: standard (executable exporter + page code, additive store field, parser-version bump). Findings: 0 CRITICAL, 0 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 0 LOW across correctness, security (code-level), maintainability and test-adequacy. The four detectors, the age bound, both caps, the drop order, the filter-independent panel, the empty state and XSS handling match the spec. D3 reads only toolDenialKind, with no string matching, and yields zero items when the field is absent. The panel ignores the session filter (filterSessions() is scoped by project/unlinked, not by sel). Every piece of transcript text goes through esc(); md() is used only for the D4 repo-text rows. Production comments contain no process narration. The one MEDIUM: the owner-message predicate counts two Claude Code synthetic user records as the owner. Measured on the owner transcripts, that clears 2 of 2 user-rejected refusals 1 ms after they occur and 3 of 11 automode-blocked refusals at a later context compaction. As a result, owner decision 1b is not delivered in practice, and 1a is only partly delivered. Deviation assessment: all eight flagged builder choices are justified-improvements (see follow_ups). The compaction limit the builder noted is the MEDIUM finding. Verification: tier 3 re-run on 8a59caa matches the claim: tests 392 OK, local/tests 304 OK (includes the exporter-conformance check, which accepts the new field because records.validate() allows unlisted fields), node tests/page.test.mjs exit 0 (131 checks). Flag-only: nothing edited, committed, pushed or deployed apart from this findings file. Verdict GO-WITH-CONDITIONS: the condition is fixing CR-009-1.

findings.title: Claude Code synthetic user records count as the owner being present, so every measured user-rejected refusal is cleared 1 ms after it happens and auto-mode refusals vanish at the next context compaction. The owner decisions to list both kinds are largely undone.

subject.name: is_owner_message(), which add_waiting() calls at line 519 to advance lastOwnerAt

evidence.value: is_owner_message accepts any user record with isMeta not True whose string content, or list text block, does not start with <. It has no exclusion for compaction summaries (isCompactSummary: true, string content) or for the interruption marker Claude Code writes as a list text block: [Request interrupted by user for tool use].

evidence.field: measurement (read-only scan of the 24 local main transcripts, driving the candidate derive.py)
evidence.value: Records the predicate classes as owner messages: 370 typed, 18 interruption markers, 8 compaction summaries. Of 15 denial records, the first owner-classified record after each was: user-rejected -> interruption marker 2/2 (1 ms later, later()==True); automode-blocked -> compaction summary 3/11 (57 min to 2 h 40 min later); the rest were typed messages.

Compaction summaries carry isCompactSummary: true. In this corpus, typed owner messages all carry permissionMode (370/370) and the interruption markers and compaction summaries carry none (0/26). That field is undocumented, so treat it as a candidate signal, not a contract.

findings.impact: The owner answered spec rows 1a and 1b on 2026-09-19: list automode-blocked and user-rejected refusals, cleared by a later owner message or by the 48-hour bound. In practice, a user-rejected refusal is always followed by the Claude Code interruption marker, which clears it at once, so that kind is effectively never shown. An automode-blocked refusal in a long autonomous run is silently cleared by the next auto-compaction while the owner is away. That is exactly the case the owner asked to see, and 27% of the measured automode-blocked refusals hit it. Spec section 1.1 treats this direction (the panel fires too rarely and asserts nothing is waiting) as the worse failure. The spec intent for the predicate is a record the owner actually typed, and these records are not typed by the owner. The unit tests pass only because no fixture places a synthetic record after a denial.
findings.remediation: Make is_owner_message() reject both synthetic record kinds. For compaction summaries, check the structural flag (isCompactSummary is True). For the interruption marker, either reject the fixed synthetic text Claude Code writes, which is a narrow exclusion on the owner predicate and not string matching on the refusal signal (the spec forbids that only for D3), or use a structural discriminator if one proves stable. Say in the docstring why each is excluded. Add regression tests in tests/test_derive.py: a user-rejected denial followed by the interruption marker still lists; an automode-blocked denial followed by a compaction summary still lists; a typed reply after either still clears; an Esc interruption with no refusal does not create an item. Remove the builder known limit (compaction clears items) once this is fixed.

add_waiting() now uses every tool_use id and tool_result tool_use_id as a dict/set key, so a malformed unhashable id would fail that session parse (the exporter keeps its last export). Claude Code does not write that shape, so this is not a finding. The tools map also keeps every call id for the life of the session in the collector stored state. It is modest in size today, and it could keep only what denials need.
